method: Node v24.15.0, three alternating fresh-process pairs per host for full compiled, full reference and cutoff comparison. All execute full N=7^13. Before uses frozen299a5a00 runtime and original source; after uses new source on the same runtime code. Cutoff compares the final source with explicit old-size prefix vs automatic half prefix. Parsing/analysis/execution included; startup excluded. RSS is process-lifetime peak. Foreign processes sampled each second, excluding controller ancestry; contaminated samples retained separately. Intel runs disclose ongoing ZFS scrub: pre-run idle+IOwait >=95%, no active swap I/O. This is a known-background control, not a completely idle-host guarantee. No process deadlines were used for benchmark runs.

limitations: Reference slows on Intel despite substantially lower RSS; no universal speedup is claimed.
Mac reference timing ranges overlap; small median differences are not evidence of a reliable speed improvement.
The half prefix sacrifices some Intel throughput compared with the larger modular prefix to save more memory. The explicit --limit option permits another tradeoff.
Intel benchmark background includes scheduled ZFS scrub. Pre-run CPU/swap checks and competing-process monitoring are recorded, not proof of a wholly idle machine.
One preliminary Mac original sample overlapped a local TypeScript check and was discarded. Other foreign-process rejections were also discarded and retained separately.
Exploratory single samples are separate from the final repeated series and must not be mixed into its medians.
environmentRepairs: The Intel rsync snapshot had no Git index. The differential runner needs tracked data provenance, so a local index was initialized using only paths present in both the local git ls-files manifest and the remote snapshot. The name-filtered main and fixture then passed.
